newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil up, but U.S. cargoes due by end-week.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil up, but U.S. cargoes due by end-week.

text.p: NWE gas oil premiums were steady on Wednesday as outright prices returned briefly to five-year highs, dealers said.

They said premiums may have peaked in the short term as the first U.S. arbitrage cargoes are set to hit the market at the end of this week, and five Russian cargoes are due to load from Ventspils before the end of September.
IPE October futures closed $1.75 higher at $225.00 per tonne, having peaked at $228.00 earlier.
A cargo of German heating oil traded at Oct IPE +$7.50 cif Hamburg for early October delivery, steady on Tuesday.
A Russian cargo traded at Oct IPE +$6.00 cif basis Rotterdam, also steady on previous premiums.

Barges traded up to Oct +$9.50 fob ARA for September-loading barges, and at Oct +$7.00 for early October lifting. A retailer in inland Germany said consumers had yet to make most of their winter purchases, and predicted higher prices.
"I believe the big boom is still to come," he said.

A cargo buyer of low sulphur diesel, who had previously talked prices up to Oct IPE +$17 cif Le Havre, stopped bidding into Bordeaux on Wednesday. But this did not stop a major offering a cargo from the UK at Oct +$19 cif.
